anti_overlap: fd-ecs-wasm-architecture covers ECS component design and WASM memory layout
fd-cultural-contamination covers how discoveries affect the living colony
fd-narrative-archaeology covers whether civilization lore produces compelling stories
decision_lens: Prioritize findings where the generation pipeline either (a) produces insufficient variety despite the claimed axes (era, material, medium philosophy, aesthetic mode, fate, scale), (b) has deterministic seed collisions that cause duplicate civilizations, or (c) generates on-demand content that causes frame stalls in WASM. A civilization that feels like a reskin of another is a P1; a generation stall visible to the player is P0.
focus: Whether the procedural generation pipeline for geological layers, civilizations, and artifacts produces sufficient variety without blowing the WASM memory/compute budget
name: fd-procgen-geology
persona: A procedural generation engineer who has shipped Voronoi-based terrain systems in browser games and built lazy-evaluated infinite worlds. Deep expertise in deterministic seeded generation, noise functions, and managing combinatorial explosions in constrained environments. Has worked on No Man's Sky-style systems and knows where PCG pipelines produce samey output despite large parameter spaces.
review_areas: Audit the actual combinatorial space of civilization axes (era x material x medium philosophy x aesthetic mode x fate x scale) — how many meaningfully distinct civilizations can the system produce vs. how many feel like reskins? Are any axes coupled so tightly they collapse the space?

Evaluate the lazy generation strategy: when a dig site reaches a new layer, what computation fires? Can civilization generation (Voronoi region lookup + seed derivation + axis selection + artifact template creation) complete within a single frame budget (~16ms) in WASM?

Check whether the region-based geological profile (8-15 Voronoi regions) creates enough spatial variety on a 40x30 map — with only ~100-200 tiles per region, do adjacent dig sites in the same region feel identical?

Assess the 3-7+ civilization count per map: is the lower bound (3) enough depth to reach the truly alien tier at layer 5+? What happens when a region only has 3 layers but the depth-dependent comprehension system expects 5+?
Verify that deterministic generation from region seed + coordinates produces stable results across save/load cycles and does not depend on generation order
Evaluate whether the artifact generation system (unique named objects from civilization axes) has enough combinatorial depth to avoid repetition within a single civilization output

severity_examples.condition: No budget allocation or incremental generation strategy is specified for on-demand civilization creation
severity_examples.scenario: Lazy generation of a deep civilization causes a multi-second freeze in WASM when an elf reaches a new layer

severity_examples.condition: Multiple axes are cosmetic-only and do not affect artifact properties, discoverable techniques, or faction dynamics
severity_examples.scenario: Two civilizations in the same playthrough feel functionally identical despite different axis values

severity_examples.condition: No blending or transition strategy between Voronoi regions is described
severity_examples.scenario: Region boundaries create visible seams where adjacent tiles have radically different geological profiles

success_hints: Each civilization should be describable in one sentence that no other civilization in the same playthrough also matches
Lazy generation should have a documented time budget and a fallback for when generation exceeds it (e.g., spread across multiple ticks)
The variable depth per region should create interesting strategic choices about where to dig, not just cosmetic differences
task_context: The brainstorm proposes multi-layer underground with 8-15 Voronoi geological regions, each containing 3-7+ procedurally generated civilizations defined by 6 axes. Layers generate lazily when excavation reaches them. Target is WASM browser with a 40x30 surface map. Current codebase uses a flat Grid<Terrain> with 6 terrain types and hecs ECS.
